# Learnings and mistakes

No structural facts are generated for this page; the store has no concept of a mistake, only of records, decisions and handovers. Everything here is written by hand.

## Notes (human, preserved verbatim on regeneration)

<!-- bm-human:begin -->
MISTAKES MADE AND CORRECTED THIS SESSION, each cost stated:

1. TAGGED THE WRONG COMMIT. Split the checksum manifest from the version bump
   across three commits; docs/RELEASE.md step 3 requires them in ONE commit,
   and a pinned test caught it by comparing the tag against the commit that
   last touched VERSION. Nothing was pushed, so the three were reshaped by
   soft reset into one release-cut commit. Cost: about ten minutes. Lesson:
   read the release procedure BEFORE cutting, not after a test refuses.

2. REPORTED A DEFECT THAT WAS MY OWN ERROR. Claimed `handover-ack` did not
   exist; it is a verb on bm_store.py and I ran it against bm_handover.py.
   Lesson: when a tool prints a clearing command, run it against the tool it
   names.

3. WROTE A REGRESSION TEST THAT FAILED FOR THE WRONG REASON. The first version
   failed because a fresh temp directory has no STATE.md at all, which is a
   much weaker condition than the real defect. Tightened to render the view
   first, so it fails for the actual reason. Lesson: a red test is not
   evidence until you read WHY it is red.

4. TWO SHELL SCANS REPORTED THEIR OWN LABEL, NOT THEIR RESULT. `grep ... |
   head -5 && echo FOUND` always prints FOUND, because head exits 0. Caught
   both times by reading the output rather than the label. Lesson: a check
   whose exit code comes from the last pipe stage is not a check.

LEARNINGS WORTH KEEPING:

- The handover's description of a defect can be stale. Of three defects
  carried forward, one did not reproduce at all and one had the wrong root
  cause named (any store operation that re-renders clears it, not a checkpoint
  specifically). Probe with the control before spending a night on a
  description.
- Fixing at the mutation rather than at the caller closes the class. The stale
  view bug existed because six CLI commands refreshed and one library method
  did not; putting the refresh in the method covers every future caller.
- A permission classifier refusing an action is information, not an obstacle.
  It was reported to the founder rather than worked around.
<!-- bm-human:end -->
